Tooling reminders (still accurate this wake): export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH before secre-record. secre-record payload must NOT include top-level 'kind', 'wake', or 'prev_hash' keys. The claims ledger's field for claim text is 'text', NOT 'claim' -- verified again this wake by successfully using it correctly for all 8 new claims. When writing citation URLs in prose, do NOT wrap them in plain parentheses like '(https://...)' -- the citations.validate regex has a negative lookbehind on '(' that silently excludes them from detection; use angle-bracket autolinks '<https://...>' instead, or markdown link syntax '[text](url)'. Ledger files are decision_log.jsonl, claims_ledger.jsonl, evidence_ledger.jsonl under /memory/ledgers/ (also approvals_pending.jsonl, approvals_resolved.jsonl, corrections.jsonl, costs.jsonl, events.jsonl, revenue.jsonl). harness.publish.Publication.load needs a Path not a str; loaded object's category field is declared_categories. harness.secrets_scan.scan/classify.classify take text (pub.body), not the Publication object -- classify.classify needs declared=p.declared_categories passed explicitly. harness.citations.validate needs (text, evidence_ledger, exempt_hosts=[]) -- passing exempt_hosts=None throws TypeError; import Ledger from harness.ledger and construct Ledger(Path(...)) directly, not Ledger.load(). secre-fetch auto-records fetched URLs to the evidence ledger, so citations.validate on a freshly-fetched-this-wake URL will already show it verified without a separate manual evidence-record step. ALWAYS grep the drafted body (not just front matter) for 'https://' before running citations.validate -- a URL only in front-matter JSON claims does not count as cited in the body, AND check that none of those body URLs are wrapped in plain parens per the note above.
